extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary criticism and general readers interested in Maeterlinck, mysticism, and aesthetic/philosophical essays
extracted.subtask_description: A literary-critical / philosophical essay (Bergson-style) examining Maeterlinck's themes: the mystical in everyday life, inner silence, habitual attention, and the cultivation of inner beauty. Not a how-to rubric but contains many evaluative principles about literature, moral life, and aesthetic attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery of the marvelous in the everyday (ihmeellisen ja jokapäiväisen yhteydellisyys)
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer's special gift is to find the marvelous and mysterious in ordinary, daily circumstances — to make the wondrous feel 'very real' (jotakin hyvin todellisuudentuntoista).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Maeterlinck first showed oppositions by bringing death into everyday tasks on stage; later he discovered 'järkyttäviä ihmeitä' in brighter, more ordinary things like flowers and bees. Anti-pattern: treating the marvelous as merely theatrical or divorced from mundane experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silence and inwardness as primary means of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: If we have something truly real to say to others, we should be silent; souls touch each other best without the senses. Inner vision (sisäisen näkemiskyvyn voima) is the most important force in life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoting Carlyle: 'Silence and Secrecy!' — cultivate inner silence rather than loud outward proclamation. Practical implication: value subtle, interior revelation over overt exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual practice of inner attention (not mere chance glimpses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sudden ecstatic glimpses are insufficient; the divine or the serious life must become habitual — 'sattumien on tultava tavaksi'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: train yourself to 'keep your eyes open to all lights' and make attention to beauty and depth a regular practice. Anti-pattern: relying on traumatic events (death, catastrophe) as the sole avenue to profundity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giving palpable form to high imagination and making abstract reality tangible
rubrics_metrics.description: Great writers can render highest imaginings tangible and can also provide spiritual/ideational explanations for concrete events, making the abstract feel 'kouraantuntuvaksi'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Maeterlinck describes a little dog's life or an automobile's mechanism with the same gripping interest as a human structure; successful prose makes imagination feel touchable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral seriousness and hatred of falsehood (rehellisyys)
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer or thinker should abhor falsehood and pursue honesty in purpose — Maeterlinck (like Emerson) 'valhetta kammova ja rehellinen pyrkimyksessään'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not fear apparent inconsistencies; trust the seriousness of life's pursuits. Anti-pattern: rhetorical ostentation or affectation intended to seem more marvelous than one is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity between life and work (sopusointu teosten ja elämän välillä)
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be harmony between an author's life and their works; genuine authorship is reflected in modest, orderly living that echoes the tone of their writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Maeterlinck's modest, retreating personal life (living in an old monastery, gardening, manual crafts) matches the seriousness of his books. Anti-pattern: public persona or extravagance that contradicts literary tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness to small signs and everyday tokens of the divine
rubrics_metrics.description: One should be ready to perceive the divine or the sublime in tiny, ordinary things (a word, a gesture, a drop of water) rather than demanding dramatic portents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice noticing small moments (a smile, a handshake, a passing thought). The essay repeatedly emphasizes that a single smile may reveal what catastrophe alone shows to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art's highest aim: open highways from visible to invisible
rubrics_metrics.description: Highest poetry and art aim to 'keep open those great highways which lead from the visible to the invisible' — i.e., to preserve routes from ordinary perception into deeper metaphysical truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for creators: avoid closing down silence and mystery; cultivate works that point beyond themselves toward inner, ineffable realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivation of inner beauty (sisäinen kauneus) as the soul's nourishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The soul's true nourishment is beauty; inner beauty is easily cultivated and rapidly ennobles the person — small acts and words can awaken dormant angels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical: endorse simple, regular practices that direct attention to the beautiful; a single 'noble and lofty word' spoken often can change timid souls and make everyday life more real.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer small habitual goodness over spectacular heroics
rubrics_metrics.description: Heroic or virtuous life does not require great feats; moral greatness arises from making small, virtuous actions habitual and from the ambient 'ilmapiiri' that rewards truth and beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to shift the surrounding moral atmosphere so that petty vices fall away; cultivate recurring small virtues rather than waiting for exceptional circumstances to prove character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empathic, inner-seeing love as the test of moral perception
rubrics_metrics.description: True neighbor-love is to see in others what is eternal in them; one learns to love by seeing the divine in people's inner being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training: spend interior, concentrated moments of attention on others; recognition (seeing) precedes genuine loving action. Anti-pattern: external charity unaccompanied by inner perception may be morally shallow.
